title: Enhancer x promoter multiplicativity and rank-order flips (Bergman 2022 ExP STARR-seq, K562)
converted_by: tracks/suite/make-cases.mjs; numbers are the agent's own, times are file times, see the header of that script

statement.text: Law: log2 activity(p,e) = mu + a_e + b_p, i.e. activity = enhancer strength x promoter strength. Bound: tracks/research/lean/q1-theory-lean__EnhancerPromoterRank.lean (EPSpec.no_reversal_of_monotone) and q1-mechanisms__RankSaturation.lean (Q1.no_reversal) state that any model f(p,e) = h_p(a_e) with monotone h_p (multiplicative, log-additive, promoter-specific saturation) permits zero true strict rank reversals, so reversals beyond measurement noise falsify the whole class. I read both files but did not re-compile them in this run.

items.what: In the law: exact multiplicativity, and the whole monotone single-strength class, is falsified, since 1,051 significant reversals were seen where 0 are allowed and about 25 are expected from noise. The violation is small: 0.039% of well-measured comparisons, with 83.5% of held-out variance explained.

In my own run: the first noise model (SD across the 4 RNA replicates) was wrong because the replicates share the same barcodes; it gave a spurious 7.7% flip rate in the development rehearsal. It was fixed by a timestamped amendment before the held-out data were read.

The amended barcode noise is slightly too large: the null predicts 19.5% raw discordance vs 17.9% observed, and the additive residual SD of 0.85 is below the median SE of 0.97. The z>3 test is therefore conservative and the true flip rate may be somewhat higher.
The null assumes Gaussian noise, and heavy-tailed barcode outliers could produce part of the 42-fold excess; I did not test this.

Earlier agent work: q1-data reported 26.5% reversals among doubly-significant pairs on the mouse GSE186265 data using 'pooled replicate SD' as noise. That is the same class of noise model that failed here, so that figure may be inflated; I did not re-test it.

Earlier agent work: q1-critic's arccos(rho)/pi null was only simulated, and q1-literature relayed R^2 = 0.82 without a held-out re-computation; this run is the first held-out check and it agrees (0.835).

In the Lean files: the theorem is about noise-free values, and Q1.no_reversal is over natural numbers, so it gives no quantitative noise allowance; the comparison to data needs the simulated null, which is outside Lean.

In the data and pipeline: about 6 barcodes per cell on average and many low-count cells; I used raw reads with pseudocount 1, not the authors' weighted reads or Poisson model; scrambled control sequences were kept as ordinary enhancers and promoters; 1014 enhancer ids, not 1000; flips were tested only on the 50 promoters with most DNA input, so promoter-class effects among weak promoters are not covered.
The null used only 10 simulations. No simulated data were used for any performance number.
